title: Reset-Enhanced Dissipative Quantum Metrology
authors: Silan Li, Qingjun Tong, Ruicheng Bao
abstract: Quantum metrology is ultimately shaped not only by measurements, but also by the dissipative dynamics that prepare and maintain the probe. Nevertheless, a general mechanism for enhancing both steady-state and transient precision in open quantum systems has been lacking. Here we show that adding a simple reset channel provides such a mechanism: reset acts as a minimal dissipative control that can enhance metrological precision without modifying the intrinsic Hamiltonian or applying continuous coherent driving. We derive a unified quantum-Fisher-information (QFI) reset-rate response identity, showing how reset enhances steady-state and transient estimation while revealing a sharp transient distinction. For static-parameter estimation in diagonal dynamics, reset leaves the leading short-time QFI unchanged; for the separate task of elapsed-time estimation, it generates an immediate drift contribution that can scale quadratically with the reset rate in the short-time limit. For frequency estimation, the enhancement is instead dominated by a genuinely quantum eigenvector contribution. These results establish reset as a simple dissipative resource for open-system quantum metrology.
summary: This theoretical paper demonstrates that introducing a simple reset channel into an open quantum system can serve as a minimal dissipative resource to enhance quantum metrological precision. The authors derive a general identity linking the QFI to the reset rate, showing that the benefit differs significantly between estimating static parameters versus estimating elapsed time. This establishes reset as a versatile tool for quantum sensing.
main_problem: The paper addresses the lack of a general mechanism to enhance quantum metrological precision (QFI) in open quantum systems, considering both steady-state and transient dynamics.
main_result: Adding a simple reset channel acts as a minimal dissipative control that enhances metrological precision without altering the intrinsic Hamiltonian or requiring continuous coherent driving.
method: The authors derive a unified quantum-Fisher-information (QFI) reset-rate response identity and analyze the QFI by expanding the system state and QFI in powers of the reset rate 'r'.

key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), $F[ho(t)]$, which quantifies the ultimate precision bound for parameter estimation.
important_parameters: Reset rate ($r$), system parameters ($\omega,  eta$), and time ($t$). The analysis distinguishes between static-parameter estimation and elapsed-time estimation.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on local small-reset expansions, meaning the derived enhancement conditions are local and do not guarantee global optimality.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how reset improves thermometry only in certain temperature windows, and show that time estimation benefits immediately from reset-induced drift, while static estimation benefits only at subleading time orders.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general QFI response identity, then applies it to specific estimation tasks: static parameter estimation (thermometry), elapsed-time estimation, and frequency estimation, highlighting the distinct physical mechanisms of enhancement for each.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general theoretical tool—the reset channel—to engineer enhanced sensing capabilities in realistic, dissipative quantum systems, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and quantum sensing.
